You will own the end-to-end early customer experience across web and app — spanning post-checkout confirmation, subscription management, digital engagement, and the critical Box 1→2→3 progression — across all HelloFresh Group brands, including Factor.

This role demands a PM who is obsessed with solving customer pain points and equally obsessed with the cross-squad collaboration required to do it at scale. Onboarding does not sit inside a single product surface — it spans the activation funnel, CRM and lifecycle communications, app and engagement experiences, and Data Science. • Own the product vision and strategy for the end-to-end Onboarding experience across all HelloFresh Group brands — from post-checkout confirmation to Settled Conversion (3 boxes in 4 weeks).

Role Overview

Lenovo is seeking an experienced Senior Technical Product Manager to shape the roadmap and drive delivery for our enterprise Hybrid Cloud Platform.

In this role, you will define the core capabilities that connect on-premises data centers with public clouds, giving enterprise customers a unified, reliable environment to run and manage their applications. You will focus on what to build and why-defining platform features across compute, storage, networking, and access control that make it easy for engineering teams and enterprise users to deploy workloads wherever they make the most sense.

You will treat both internal offering teams and external enterprise clients as your platform customers. Your mission is to listen to their needs, translate their technical challenges into clear product requirements, and partner with engineering squads who bring the technical architecture to life.

Key Responsibilities

1. Hybrid Cloud Strategy & Core Capabilities

• Define the product vision, roadmap, and release milestones for our hybrid cloud platform across private infrastructure and major public cloud providers.

• Specify core platform features across compute, storage, networking, and user authentication so teams can deploy and run applications seamlessly.

• Lead 0-to-1 MVP scoping for new platform releases, balancing customer-requested features against realistic delivery timelines.

2. Workload Management & Scaling

• Define requirements for workload placement, allowing customers to easily balance applications between their private environments and public cloud capacity.

• Ensure the platform provides reliable multi-tenant isolation, security policies, and health monitoring so customers trust it for production workloads.

3. Developer Experience & Customer Enablement

• Run regular discovery sessions with platform users (both internal teams and external customers) to understand integration friction and day-to-day pain points.

• Specify self-service platform tools, clear APIs, and developer documentation that make onboarding smooth and self-guided.

• Author clear Product Requirements Documents (PRDs) and user stories that outline business value and acceptance criteria for engineering teams.

4. Cloud Economics & Usage Tracking

• Define capabilities that give customers visibility into their resource usage and spending across hybrid environments.

• Specify quota controls, budget alerts, and reporting dashboards so organizations can monitor their cloud investments with confidence.

5. AI & Modern Workload Readiness

• Ensure the platform is ready to support modern workloads, including allocating GPU resources and supporting modern AI tools and data services as customer demand grows.

Required Qualifications

• 8+ Years of Product Management Experience: Must have a proven track record of owning and shipping software products from concept through launch in a dedicated Product Manager capacity.

• Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, or equivalent practical experience.

• Demonstrated Cloud Offering Ownership: Prior hands-on experience operating as a Product Manager for a commercial or enterprise cloud offering/product (public, private, or hybrid cloud environments).

• Cloud & Infrastructure Fundamentals: Solid understanding of core cloud infrastructure components (compute, storage, and networking) and how private enterprise environments connect with public cloud platforms (such as AWS, Azure, or GCP).

• Core Inbound PM Craft: Demonstrated experience gathering customer requirements, writing detailed PRDs, defining API interfaces, and prioritizing roadmaps using structured decision-making frameworks.

• Customer Empathy & Discovery: Strong background in customer discovery-uncovering underlying user needs and translating them into practical software capabilities.

• Communication & Collaboration: Exceptional cross-functional leadership skills, with the ability to bridge business goals with technical conversations and guide engineering squads toward shared outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications

• Prior product management experience at an enterprise cloud provider or software infrastructure company.

• Working knowledge of container environments (e.g., Kubernetes) or modern cloud deployment models.

• Curiosity about modern AI systems and how they utilize cloud and GPU infrastructure.

As a Senior Staff Product Manager for Adversarial Actors, you'll own the end-to-end strategy for inauthentic behavior on Pinterest. This includes detection and enforcement for bots, account takeovers, and spam across the entire Pinterest funnel. You’ll partner closely with teams across Pinterest, including Policy, Operations, Engineering, and Data Science to protect Pinners, advertisers, and the business.

What you'll do:
• Define and deliver Pinterest's company-wide adversarial strategy spanning pre-authentication, login/signup, and post-authentication surfaces — setting multi-year vision, aligning executive stakeholders, and driving coordinated investment across Policy, Ops, MLE, Integrity Analytics, Data Science, Security, and Identity.
• Develop and execute on the post-authentication roadmap, including measurement, detection signals, and enforcement actions. Support the Bots & ATO PM on pre-authentication roadmap.
• Partner with Data Science and Engineering to build spam account and domain signals, including network-based detection, ML models, and heuristic-based rules.
• Partner with the Enforcement Systems team to develop the associated suite of spam account and domain enforcement actions such as warnings, rate limits, feature restrictions, deactivations, and domain-level actions.
• Set the metrics and measurement strategy for post-authentication spam prevalence, detection quality, and enforcement effectiveness.
• Anticipate emerging adversarial patterns and continuously reprioritize investments to stay ahead of evolving abuse.

What we're looking for:
• Minimum 10 years of product management experience, with deep expertise in trust & safety, account integrity, anti-abuse, or adversarial domains
• Proven track record owning ML-powered detection products and shipping enforcement systems at scale
• Strong data fluency — comfortable with precision/recall/FPR, prevalence measurement, and reasoning about adversarial dynamics
• SQL proficiency — able to self-serve data investigation and analysis
• Demonstrated systems thinking — experience navigating complex, interconnected detection and enforcement infrastructure
• Exceptional cross-functional leadership and executive-level communication — proven ability to drive alignment and decisions across functions, and present strategy and recommendations to all levels of leadership.
• Strong judgment on policy and enforcement tradeoffs, balancing enforcement with false-positive user impact
• Excellent written and verbal communication of complex adversarial, ML, and policy concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field such as Computer Science, or equivalent experience

RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile.
We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $16B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.
We're a remote-first team of 150+ people across 25+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance.
This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.
The RoleAs Senior Product Manager, User Acquisition, you'll explore an important extension of how RevenueCat helps developers grow: helping them not just monetize the users they have, but acquire more of the right users in the first place.
RevenueCat already has several footholds in user acquisition, including our Apple Ads integration and integrations across the attribution and MMP ecosystem. But we're still early in defining what a broader RevenueCat user acquisition product should become. You'll be the first dedicated product hire focused on this space, reporting directly to our product lead for Ads, with significant latitude to shape both the strategy and the products we build.
This is a genuine zero-to-one role. You won't inherit a predetermined roadmap. Your job will be to deeply understand how app developers acquire users today, identify where RevenueCat has an opportunity to solve problems meaningfully better, and turn those insights into products we can test, ship, and scale.
You'll bring real expertise in mobile performance marketing and user acquisition to that process. The opportunity could eventually span attribution and measurement, products built on top of existing acquisition channels, new ways to optimize spend using downstream monetization data, partnerships, advertising infrastructure, or things we haven't considered yet. We have hypotheses, but we're hiring you in part because we want your perspective on which ones are worth pursuing.
RevenueCat has some unusual advantages to build from: relationships with a large ecosystem of app developers, deep visibility into subscription and monetization outcomes, infrastructure already embedded in apps, and a growing advertising business. The challenge is figuring out how those assets can translate into something uniquely valuable for developers trying to grow.
About you:• You have 5+ years of experience owning meaningful product or growth decisions end-to-end. Your title may have been Product Manager, founder, growth leader, or something else — what's important is that you've been accountable for deciding what to build and whether it worked.

• You have deep, hands-on experience with mobile user acquisition—either directly managing and optimizing acquisition for mobile apps, or building products and infrastructure used by mobile acquisition teams. You understand how app developers actually acquire users, measure performance, and make decisions about where to spend their next dollar.

• You understand the modern mobile acquisition stack, including MMPs and attribution, Apple Ads, Meta and Google advertising products, conversion APIs, and related measurement infrastructure.

• You can reason clearly about attribution, performance-marketing economics, and privacy. You understand concepts such as CAC, LTV, ROAS, optimization signals, ATT, SKAdNetwork/AdAttributionKit, consent management, and how downstream behavior should influence acquisition decisions.

• You thrive in zero-to-one environments. You can take a large, ambiguous opportunity, identify the most important unanswered questions, narrow it into product bets, and find pragmatic ways to test those bets before making large investments.

• You are sufficiently technical to work closely with engineering on integrations, APIs, SDKs, data flows, identity, attribution, and other technical product decisions.

• You communicate clearly across different audiences and media, particularly in writing.

In the first month, you'll:• Spend significant time with developers understanding how they acquire users today, how they evaluate acquisition performance, and where the process is painful, expensive, fragmented, or opaque.

• Build a deep understanding of RevenueCat's existing acquisition-related products, integrations, data, customer research, and technical capabilities.

• Build strong working relationships with engineering, design, data, go-to-market, and other product teams whose work intersects with user acquisition.

• Develop a clear picture of the acquisition ecosystem, the problems RevenueCat is particularly well positioned to solve, and the biggest assumptions we still need to test.

• Begin forming your own point of view on where RevenueCat could create differentiated value in user acquisition.

Within the first 3 months, you'll:• Have narrowed the broad user acquisition opportunity into a small number of concrete product hypotheses, grounded in customer research, market understanding, and RevenueCat's unique advantages.

• Have a clear recommendation for where we should focus first — and why.

• Begin validating that direction through prototypes, design partners, technical exploration, lightweight product experiments, or an initial shippable bet.

• Establish a learning agenda that makes the biggest risks and unanswered questions explicit, and gives us a fast path to increasing or decreasing our conviction.

• Align senior stakeholders around what we're testing, what we're not pursuing yet, and what evidence would cause us to change direction.

Within the first 6 months, you'll:• Have shipped our first substantive user acquisition product bet, or generated enough evidence to decisively change or stop it before making a larger investment.

• Have real evidence from the market about where RevenueCat can — and cannot — create differentiated value.

• Be independently driving product discovery, prioritization, and execution for the user acquisition area.

• Have developed an evidence-backed point of view on the most promising opportunities in the space and what capabilities RevenueCat would need to pursue them.

• Have turned a broad strategic opportunity into an increasingly focused product direction.

Within the first 12 months, you'll:• Have established a clear strategic direction for RevenueCat in user acquisition, supported by customer behavior and product evidence rather than thesis alone.

• Have shipped meaningful products or experiments that either created measurable value for developers or materially changed our understanding of the opportunity—including changing or killing bets when the evidence didn’t support them.

• Have a credible longer-term roadmap for turning the strongest early signals into a meaningful RevenueCat product area.

• Be the primary IC product owner for User Acquisition and the internal domain expert on how app developers acquire, measure, and optimize users.

• Have helped define how RevenueCat's monetization data, developer footprint, and advertising capabilities can work together to create a differentiated position in app growth.

What we offer:• Competitive equity in a fast-growing, Series C startup backed by top-tier investors, including Y Combinator

• 10-year window to exercise vested equity options

• A fully remote environment designed around autonomy and flexibility

• 4-5 weeks of flexible time off annually

• Paid desk at a co-working space

• Workspace budget and continuous learning stipend
